neighbours.label: Word right after a negation, mainly ' time' in 'wasted no time' / 'not enough time', also stems completing un- words (unseemly, ungodly, unsurprisingly) and 'not improbable'
fire: The new coach wasted no time in rearranging the lineup before the first match of the season.
We did not have enough time to finish the survey before the library closed on Friday.
The senator wasted no time responding to the accusations that appeared in the morning papers.
Students often say there is never enough time to revise properly during the busy exam weeks.
The plumber had no time to fix the leak because another emergency call came in.
It would not take much time to repair the fence if everyone helped out together.
The unseemly behaviour of the guests at the wedding was not forgotten for a long time.
The ungodly noise from the construction site woke the whole street at dawn.
quiet: The new coach rearranged the lineup carefully before the first match of the season began.
We finished the survey early and walked to the library before it closed on Friday.
The senator responded to the accusations in a long interview with the morning papers.
Students often revise for weeks during the busy exam period and feel well prepared.
The plumber arrived quickly and fixed the leak in about twenty minutes.
The gentle rain fell over the quiet garden while the children played inside.
The guests behaved politely at the wedding and everyone danced until midnight.
The construction crew started at dawn and the noise carried across the street.

notes: Label and sentences written blind by a Claude subagent from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt.md, identical for Haiku, Sonnet and Opus); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus comparison on the same 48 poles.
